briefing.headline: Moving from two to three office days is predicted to raise leavers over the next 12 months from 641 to 893, about 250 more people or a 39% increase, with mood clearly negative (-0.79 on a -2 to +2 scale).
briefing.most_at_risk: Caregivers (+51%, 1,650 people) and long commuters (+48%, 3,000 people, 60% of staff) react worst, along with mid-level staff and managers (+47–48% versus +32% for juniors), while short-commute staff barely mind (+24%) because one extra 15–30 minute trip changes little for them.
risks: The exception process carries most of the caregiver risk: the long-commute parents quoted say they will apply and wait, and one says outright she will start looking if HR says no, so a slow or stingy process could turn waiting into resignations.

Almost every voice with a 30+ minute commute says they will 'keep an eye on' hybrid competitors, so this policy creates a pool of passive job-seekers that active recruiters can easily convert, even if most stay at first.

The higher loss rates among mid-level staff and managers, about 1 in 2.8 of the extra leavers coming from the 750 managers alone if rates hold, would cost more in client continuity and replacement than the junior headline suggests.
design_changes: Open exception applications now, publish clear approval criteria for caring and health needs, and give decisions before the policy starts so no one spends the first weeks of the quarter waiting and job-hunting.

Before launch, check that shuttle routes actually cover where the 3,000 long commuters live (80–90 minutes each way in the voices), and let teams set office-day start and end times to avoid peak traffic and fit late client calls.

Phase in the third day or pilot it with a few teams, and commit publicly to a review date using actual resignation and exception data, since several voices say they would only leave 'if they keep tightening it.'
briefing.confidence: medium, the direction and the ranking of groups are consistent across every cut and match the voices, but with only 48 modelled voices (about two per group) treat the extra 250 leavers as a rough range, not a forecast.
